title: 2025 New York City Electrical Code (NYC amendments to the 2020 NEC, incl. administrative sections EC 80-87)
keyFacts: §28-1101.1 adopts the 2020 edition of NFPA 70 subject to NYC amendments; together cited as the 'New York city electrical code' (p.1).
§28-1101.2: commissioner must propose an update to the latest NEC no later than the 3rd year after the effective date and every 3rd year thereafter (p.1).
EC 84.5: a master electrician business or special electrician filing a permit for work installed by an unlicensed person must state that on the application (p.4).

EC 84.6: 1-4 family dwellings - a one-family residence may have only 1 utility meter; 2+ units get 1 meter per dwelling unit plus 1 optional common-area meter (smoke detection required in common areas) (p.4).
EC 84.7: applications to energize wiring/meters must include a statement signed and sealed by the master or special electrician that the owner authorized the work in writing (p.4).

EC 86.1-86.4: permitted electrical work is inspected by DOB (except minor electrical work); permit holder schedules the final inspection and keeps work accessible; DOB issues sign-off after passing (pp.4-5).
110.2(B): DOB submission/approval required for installations of 1000 kVA or larger (service, transformers, UPS, generators, ESS, PV, etc.) and any installation above 1000 V AC / 1500 V DC (pp.6-7).
110.3(D) new: electrical equipment rooms must be dedicated, identified, not used for storage; all equipment in them installed by a licensed electrician (p.7).
210.11(C)(5)/210.52(J) new: living rooms, bedrooms, dining rooms need at least 1 air-conditioner receptacle on an individual branch circuit, unless central A/C serves the room (pp.9-10).
210.12(A) Exception No. 2: AFCI not required for kitchen receptacles and laundry-equipment receptacles in multifamily dwellings over 3 stories (p.9).
210.19(A)/215.2(A)(1): 5% maximum combined feeder + branch voltage drop is mandatory; minimum dwelling-unit feeder is 3 conductors of 8 AWG Cu or 6 AWG Al/Cu-clad Al (pp.9-10).

230.43: service-entrance conductors limited to RMC, IMC, EMT, metal wireways, busways, metal aux gutters, PVC (per 230.6), cable bus; exposed PVC service masts allowed on residential buildings within 3,000 ft of salt water (p.14).
334.10/334.12: NM cable permitted in 1-2 family and multifamily dwellings but prohibited in dwellings/garages exceeding 3 floors above grade and in non-residential buildings (p.20).
330.12: MC not permitted as service conductors; PVC-jacketed MC prohibited in buildings over 3 floors unless concealed in 1-hour rated non-plenum assemblies (p.20).
382.12 and 394.12: nonmetallic extensions and concealed knob-and-tube wiring not permitted (pp.23-24).
notes: Footer date 2025.12.21. Amendment-only document (does not reproduce the full NEC). Article 230.71 retains the 2020 NEC 'two to six disconnects' language as amended (pp.16-17). Energy storage systems section begins p.49. Text extraction loses formatting; consult PDF for exact wording.

title: NYC Local Law 128 of 2024 (enacts NYC Electrical Code into Title 28; licensing Articles 429/430; permits/minor electrical work)
publisher: New York City Council / Office of the City Clerk (hosted by DOB)
keyFacts: §29: takes effect 1 year after becoming law, for applications filed on/after that date; owner may opt in earlier (new buildings; existing buildings within 120 days) (p.109).
Passed by Council Nov 21, 2024; returned unsigned by the Mayor Dec 23, 2024 (p.109).

§28-101.5 'Minor electrical work' = 11 categories incl. replacing defective breakers/switches <=30 A (not main disconnect), replacing up to 5 fixtures in existing outlets without increasing wattage, installing 10 or fewer units not requiring a new branch circuit, transformers <=1000 VA (p.2).
§28-105.2 item 13: electrical permits required for electrical work other than low-voltage work, including minor electrical work (p.4).

§28-105.4.7: no permit for <50 V signaling/communication/alarm/data wiring done by a master/special electrician or qualified person; life-safety, hazardous-location, intrinsically safe systems and connections to light/heat/power control circuits are reserved to licensed electricians (p.5).
§28-105.5.1 exception: the electrical permit applicant must be the licensed master or special electrician who performs the work (p.6).
§28-116.2.4 exception: no final inspection for minor electrical work (p.7).

§28-429.1: unlawful to perform electrical work unless a licensed master electrician or under direct and continuing supervision of one (exceptions: low-voltage by qualified persons; special electricians) (p.13).

§28-429.3.1: master license experience - 7 of last 10 years with tools under a licensed master/special electrician in the US, at least 2 years in NYC (alternatives: EE degree + 3 yrs; NYS DOL-registered apprenticeship + 5 yrs; inspector credit up to 2.5 yrs) (p.14).

§28-429.7: master electrician must establish a master electrician business with a place of business in NYC; no business may use 'electric/electrical' in its name unless it is a master electrician business (p.15).
notes: 110 pages. Contains the same NEC amendment text as the DOB consolidated code plus the administrative/licensing amendments. No out-of-state reciprocity provision was found.

title: NYC Local Law 42 of 2026 (conforming amendments re Existing Building Code; electrical and elevator inspections)
publisher: New York City Council / Office of the City Clerk (hosted by DOB)
keyFacts: §§150-151 amend EC 86.1/86.2: permitted electrical work (except minor electrical work) is inspected 'as directed by the commissioner'; final inspection required where required by code or DOB rules (pp.87-88).
§153: §28-116.2.6.4 and §§150-151 take effect immediately; §152 (elevator) on Jan 1, 2027; the rest 18 months after becoming law (pp.88-89).
Passed by Council Dec 18, 2025; returned unsigned by the Mayor Jan 20, 2026 (p.89).
New §28-116.2.6.4: final inspections for electrical work requiring a permit follow the NYC Electrical Code (p.26).
notes: Mixed status: electrical-inspection sections in force since early 2026; most other provisions pending (~18 months after Jan 2026, i.e. around mid-2027 - computed, not stated). effectiveDate left null because it varies by section.

title: DOB Electrical Code web page
keyFacts: States the 2025 NYC Electrical Code took full effect on December 21, 2025 and consists of Title 28 administrative amendments plus NYC amendments to the 2020 NEC (page text).

Electrical Plan Review required for installations >=1000 kVA or new/revised installations above 600 V, submitted by a NYS-licensed PE or RA (page text; note the code text itself says above 1000 V AC/1500 V DC).
Electrical Equipment Review by DOB OTCR required for equipment without an acceptable testing-laboratory label (page text).
notes: Web page; minor discrepancy (600 V on page vs 1000 V in EC 110.2(B)(5)).

title: DOB Electrical Work Guidance Document (with Buildings Bulletin 2025-008)
keyFacts: Three filing categories: Minor Electrical Work (permit, no DOB inspection or plan review); Electrical Work (permit + DOB inspection, no plan review); Electrical Work incl. Special Installations per EC 110.2(B) (plan review + permit + inspection) (p.1 of guide / PDF p.2).
Plan review submissions go to elecplanreview@buildings.nyc.gov, signed by a PE/RA (or engineer licensed in any state/foreign jurisdiction), $650 per submission (PDF p.3).
A PE-prepared selective coordination report must be filed before electrical inspection where required (PDF p.5).

title: DOB NOW: Build Electrical Filings FAQs
keyFacts: Standalone electrical filings (no linked DOB NOW job) can only select '2020 NEC / 2025 NYC Electrical Code' (FAQ, code selection).
Filings linked to existing jobs may show '2008 NEC / 2011 NYC Electrical Code' or '2020 NEC / 2025 NYC Electrical Code' (FAQ).
Electrical inspection requests are made in DOB NOW: Inspections Plus; parts fees are paid in DOB NOW rather than deducted from firm accounts for permits after June 29, 2026 (FAQ, payments).
notes: Web page; FAQ content changes frequently.

title: Obtain a Master & Special Electrician License (DOB)
keyFacts: Must pass written ($585) then practical ($530) exam before the background application; written is multiple choice on NYC codes, closed book, 70% to pass (Step 1).
24 months from written-exam notification to pass the practical; 1 year from practical notification to file the license application in DOB NOW: Licensing (Steps 1-2).

Eligibility: at least 18, good moral character, and the 7-of-10-years experience rule with at least 2 years in NYC under a licensed master/special electrician (or the degree/apprenticeship/inspector alternatives) (eligibility section).
Experience proven with Experience Verification Forms signed by supervisors and Social Security itemized earnings statements; physical exam form LIC62 (required documents).
Electrician businesses must carry general liability, workers' compensation and disability insurance (business section).
notes: No reciprocity/out-of-state license transfer pathway is described on this page; out-of-state experience counts only if under a licensed master/special electrician in the US and still requires 2 NYC years.

title: DOB NOW: Licensing Winter 2026 Release - Electrician Licenses industry session
keyFacts: Special Electrician = individual authorized to do electrical work in/on specific buildings while employed by the building owner (p.6).
Civil Service special electricians submit a Civil Service exam report instead of written/practical exams (p.6).
Written exam fee $585, practical exam fee $530 (p.9).
Licenses can be renewed starting 90 days before expiration; late fees apply (p.103).
notes: 160-page slide deck, mostly DOB NOW UI screenshots.

title: DOB: Changes to Electrical License (business changes, shelving, unshelving)
keyFacts: Corporations/LLCs for an electrical business must have 'Electric/Electrical' in the firm name and an all-purpose clause stating the company is formed to do electrical work (page text).
Shelving a license requires closing/transferring open jobs and surrendering license and seal; unshelving requires proof of industry involvement while shelved (page text).
notes: Some references still cite former §27-3013 (pre-2025 code).

title: NYS DOS informational announcement: Adoption of the 2025 Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code
publisher: NYS Department of State, Division of Building Standards and Codes
keyFacts: Code Council adopted the 2025 Uniform Code on July 25, 2025, repealing the 2020 edition (p.1).
Effective date of the 2025 Uniform Code is December 31, 2025; permit applications from that date must comply (p.1).
notes: Manufactured-housing announcement; does not itself name the NEC edition. necEdition '2023' is from nys-2025-energy-code-rule-text. Obtained via WebFetch (direct download blocked). DOS notice page (https://dos.ny.gov/notice-adoption) says a transition period allowed either 2020 or 2025 Uniform Code (read via WebFetch summary only; not saved). The Uniform Code does not govern NYC, which has its own construction codes - not confirmed from a saved state source.

title: NYS 19 NYCRR Part 1240 rule text (2025 State Energy Conservation Construction Code)
keyFacts: Part 1240 incorporates by reference NFPA '70-23 National Electric Code' (pp.7 and 13).
notes: Only an indirect confirmation of the NEC edition used by NY State (energy code reference). The Uniform Code's own referenced-standards listing (2025 Building/Residential Code of NYS) was not retrieved because those books are ICC-hosted.

title: NYS Regulatory Impact Statement for the 2025 Uniform Code rulemaking (Appendix B)
keyFacts: States the Uniform Code incorporates many NFPA references by reference, including the National Electric Code (NFPA 70) (p.4).
notes: Proposal-stage document (June 2025); edition of NFPA 70 not stated in the extracted text. Background only.

title: Con Edison Electric Service Requirements ('Blue Book'), 2026 Edition (revised May 2026)
publisher: Consolidated Edison Company of New York
keyFacts: Cover: Revised May 2026, 2026 Edition, supersedes all previous editions (p.2).
Customer must request a Con Edison final inspection via the Final Inspection Checklist; meter work order issues only after the final inspection passes with no deficiencies (Step 5).

Contractor must obtain the AHJ's certificate of inspection; an electric certificate is generally required for addition, alteration, installation, repair etc. of customer-owned wiring (Section O, p.28).
Con Edison inspects from point of service termination through service and meter equipment (Section P, p.28).
notes: Utility document, read but not stored (copyright). 104 pages.
